mainTopic: 高中新生活的挑战与成长
mainTopicEn: Challenges and Growth in High School Life
mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕"开学"话题，涵盖校长致辞（潜力与挑战）、校园生活、社团活动和适应新环境四个子话题，是高考写作和雅思议论文的核心命题范畴。

subTopics.title: 潜力开发与个人成长
subTopics.desc: 校长开学致辞的核心话题：认识潜力、迎接挑战、实现个人成长。

prompts.task: 假设你是校英文报主编李华，你报正举办以"Unlocking Your Potential"为主题的征文活动。请你写一篇短文投稿，内容包括：1. 你对"潜力"的理解；2. 你或身边人释放潜力的一次经历；3. 你的收获与感悟。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference: Potential is not about what you are born with, but about what you are willing to become. I still remember the first time I rose to the challenge of public speaking. My heart was racing and my hands were shaking, but I told myself that this was my opportunity to acquire a skill I desperately wanted. The path before me was full of challenges — new techniques, unfamiliar audiences, and the fear of failure. Yet the moment I finished my speech, I realized I had taken the first step towards becoming a more confident version of myself. In time, I found myself growing into someone who actually enjoyed sharing ideas. As our principal said, potential is your natural ability that can be developed when you try hard enough. All it takes is the courage to start and the determination to persist.

prompts.task: Some people believe that talent is innate and cannot be taught, while others argue that any skill can be developed through practice and education. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons and examples. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
The question of whether exceptional ability is a gift bestowed at birth or a product of sustained effort has long divided opinion. While some maintain that genuine talent is inborn and beyond the reach of instruction, others insist that virtually any competence can be cultivated through disciplined practice and sound education. Although I recognise the influence of natural aptitude, I ultimately side with the latter position.

Those who champion the idea of innate talent point to the striking ease with which certain individuals master demanding disciplines. A child who intuitively grasps musical harmony or absorbs a foreign language with little apparent struggle seems to confirm that some capacities are simply hardwired. From this perspective, no amount of coaching can transform an ordinary learner into a prodigy, because the decisive spark is inherited rather than acquired.

The opposing camp, however, argues that skill is overwhelmingly the fruit of deliberate training. Countless high achievers, from elite athletes to accomplished scientists, attribute their success not to a mysterious endowment but to years of relentless repetition, expert guidance and a willingness to learn from failure. According to this reasoning, what observers mistake for raw talent is often the invisible accumulation of thousands of hours of practice.

In my view, the second argument is considerably more persuasive. Natural predisposition may offer a head start, yet it rarely flourishes without cultivation, and history is full of celebrated figures who were initially dismissed as unremarkable. Given that structured education can extend opportunity to anyone prepared to persevere, I firmly believe that ability is developed far more than it is inherited. Talent, in essence, sets the stage, but effort writes the performance.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):完整回应了 discuss both views + own opinion 三个部分——引言 paraphrase 题目并亮明立场('I ultimately side with the latter position'),第二段客观陈述'天赋天生论'及其理由,第三段陈述'后天习得论'并展开,末段清晰权衡后重申立场('the second argument is considerably more persuasive')。立场全篇一致,论据是展开的推演(head start→需 cultivation→history 反例)而非要点罗列。

Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性与准确性):句式灵活多样——让步状语从句('Although I recognise...')、定语从句('the striking ease with which...')、分词/介词短语后置修饰、倒装式强调('what observers mistake for raw talent is...')、非谓语('a willingness to learn from failure');绝大多数句子零错误,标点规范。

subTopics.title: 校园生活与人际关系
subTopics.desc: 以定语从句为核心语法点，描述高中新生活中的人、事和情感体验。

prompts.task: 你的英国笔友Chris即将进入高中，写信向你询问高中生活的感受和建议。请你写一封回信，内容包括：1. 你进入高中后的感受；2. 你遇到的困难及如何克服；3. 给Chris的建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Chris,

I'm delighted to hear that you're starting high school soon, and I'd love to share my experience with you.

To be honest, the first month was both exciting and overwhelming. The school, which is much bigger than my junior high, felt like a maze. The teachers, who were all incredibly supportive, encouraged us to explore our interests. I've made friends with classmates whose passions range from robotics to creative writing — every day in their company is a new adventure.

Of course, there were challenges. The workload, which was heavier than I expected, took some getting used to. But I learned to manage my time through careful planning. My advice is simple: never hesitate to reach out when you need help, and always keep a positive attitude. I'm confident that you, too, will find yourself growing into a more capable and confident person.

Best wishes,
Li Hua

prompts.task: Some people think that school is the most important period of a person's life, while others believe that life after school brings more valuable experiences. Discuss both views and give your opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
The question of which stage of life shapes us most profoundly is a perennial one. While some regard formal schooling as the defining chapter of a person's existence, others argue that the years that follow it yield richer and more meaningful lessons. Having weighed both positions, I am inclined to believe that the experiences gained after school ultimately prove more valuable.

Those who champion the primacy of school do so with good reason. The classroom is where a person first acquires literacy, numeracy and the habits of disciplined thought, all of which serve as the foundation for everything that comes later. Just as a building cannot stand without solid footings, an adult cannot function without the intellectual and social groundwork laid during these formative years. Moreover, school is where children forge their earliest friendships and learn to navigate rules, competition and cooperation, thereby shaping their character at its most impressionable stage.

The opposing camp, however, contends that genuine growth begins only once the protective walls of the institution fall away. Life beyond the school gates confronts individuals with responsibilities that no lesson can fully replicate: earning a living, sustaining relationships and recovering from failure. A graduate who loses a first job, for instance, learns resilience in a way that no examination could ever teach.

On balance, although schooling is undeniably indispensable, I maintain that post-school life offers the more transformative education. The wider world demands that we apply, adapt and sometimes discard what we were taught, and it is precisely this constant testing against reality that turns knowledge into genuine wisdom.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):完整回应了 discuss both views + give your opinion 三个部分。引言明确点出立场("I am inclined to believe that the experiences gained after school ultimately prove more valuable"),第2、3段客观陈述双方看法并各自展开一个通用论据(地基比喻论证学校打基础、丢掉第一份工作学到 resilience 的假设情景),结尾段权衡后重申并论证立场,观点全篇一致、不骑墙。

Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性与准确性):句式多样且准确,含定语从句(where a person first acquires...)、比较状语从句(Just as a building cannot stand...)、分词状语(Having weighed both positions)、让步复合句(although schooling is undeniably indispensable, I maintain that...)以及强调结构(it is precisely this constant testing...that...),绝大多数句子零错误。

subTopics.title: 课外活动与社团建设
subTopics.desc: 围绕社团提案书展开，涉及规划能力、兴趣发展和校园文化建设的写作。

prompts.task: 你校国际部将成立一个新的学生社团，现面向全校征集提案。请你写一封提案信，内容包括：1. 你想成立的社团名称及理由；2. 社团的主要活动规划；3. 预期成果。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Student Council,

I am writing to propose the establishment of a Creative Writing Club, which I believe will benefit students who are passionate about storytelling in English.

The club, which would meet twice a week, will focus on three main areas. First, we will hold writing workshops where members can share their work and receive constructive feedback. Second, we will invite guest speakers — local authors and journalists — to inspire us with their techniques and experiences. Third, we plan to publish a monthly online newsletter to showcase our members' best pieces.

I am confident that this club will help students develop their writing skills, discover their creative potential, and build a community of like-minded learners. The possibilities are endless when young writers support each other. With your approval, I would be ready to launch the club early next month.

Yours sincerely,
Li Hua

prompts.task: Some people believe that schools should focus primarily on academic achievement, while others argue that extracurricular activities are equally important. Discuss both views and give your opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
There is an ongoing debate about whether schools ought to concentrate mainly on academic performance or place equal weight on activities beyond the classroom, such as sport, music and clubs. While I acknowledge the value of strong academic results, I firmly believe that extracurricular pursuits deserve comparable importance in a well-rounded education.

Those who champion academic achievement argue that a school's core mission is to equip young people with knowledge and intellectual skills. From this perspective, examinations and qualifications act as gateways to higher education and rewarding careers, so anything that diverts time from studying is a distraction. A teenager who devotes long hours to mathematics and science, rather than to hobbies, is likely to secure a university place and, ultimately, greater financial security. Given how fiercely competitive the modern job market has become, this emphasis on measurable results is understandable.

Advocates of extracurricular activities, on the other hand, contend that personal development matters just as much as grades. Team sports, debating and volunteering cultivate qualities that examinations rarely assess, including leadership, cooperation and resilience. A student who captains a football team, for instance, learns to motivate others and cope with pressure, skills that prove invaluable in adult life. Employers increasingly value such attributes, precisely because they cannot be measured by a certificate alone.

In my view, the two priorities are not mutually exclusive but complementary. An education fixated solely on grades risks producing capable yet one-dimensional individuals, whereas activities outside lessons nurture the emotional and social maturity that academic study overlooks. Schools should therefore treat both as essential, since genuine success depends on developing the whole person, not merely a high-achieving mind.

subTopics.title: 适应新环境与自我成长
subTopics.desc: 通过 John Li 的故事探讨转学适应、文化冲突和新生活的勇气。

prompts.task: 假设你是李华，你的澳大利亚朋友Alice即将到你所在城市的高中学习一年，她来信表达了对适应新环境的担忧。请你写一封回信，内容包括：1. 表示理解和安慰；2. 结合自身经历提供建议；3. 表达祝愿。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Alice,

I completely understand how you feel. Moving to a new school, especially one in a different country, can be overwhelming. When I first entered senior high, I also found everything unfamiliar — new teachers, new classmates, and a curriculum that was far more demanding than what I was used to.

The good news is that in time you will find yourself adapting naturally. When I look back, the key was to stay open and curious. I joined a few clubs, which helped me meet people who shared my interests. I also made a point of talking to my teachers whenever I felt lost — they were always willing to help. At first, there was not as much free time as I was used to, but it was still manageable with proper planning.

I have confidence in your ability to make a difference in your new environment. The challenges you face now will become the stories you tell with pride later. I'm looking forward to showing you around when you arrive!

Yours,
Li Hua

prompts.task: Moving to a new school or city can be a challenging experience for young people. What are the main difficulties they face, and what can schools and parents do to help them adapt? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Relocating to an unfamiliar school or city is often a demanding transition for adolescents. This essay will examine the principal obstacles they encounter and outline the practical measures that both schools and parents can take to ease their adjustment.

The most immediate challenge is social isolation. Having left behind established friendships, newcomers frequently struggle to break into existing peer groups, and this sense of not belonging can breed loneliness and anxiety. A second difficulty is academic disruption, since different institutions follow distinct curricula and teaching styles. A student who was thriving in one environment may suddenly find the pace unfamiliar or the material misaligned with what they previously covered, which can erode their confidence and motivation.

Schools and parents can address these problems in complementary ways. To counter social isolation, schools might implement structured buddy systems that pair each arrival with a welcoming classmate, alongside clubs and group activities that create natural opportunities for friendship. Parents, meanwhile, can encourage their children to participate and can nurture connections outside the classroom, perhaps through community sports or hobbies. As for academic difficulties, teachers can conduct early assessments to identify gaps and offer targeted support, while parents can maintain close communication with staff and provide a stable, reassuring atmosphere at home so that setbacks are treated as temporary rather than defining.

In conclusion, the chief hurdles for young people who move are forming new friendships and coping with unfamiliar academic demands. Through coordinated effort, schools can foster inclusion and learning support while parents supply emotional stability. With such backing, most adolescents will ultimately adapt and even flourish in their new surroundings.
